description:
Building the Space Mission Design Game for NASA Space Apps—an interactive web simulation using React & Tailwind.

Looking for teammates interested in Frontend/UI, Game Logic, or Space Science. All skill levels welcome—join us!
summary:
Horizon-X is a browser-native 3D aerospace engineering simulation and educational mission 
design game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Traditional space mission design 
is historically locked behind dense academic handbooks and siloed simulation tools. Horizon
X bridges this gap by placing players directly into a virtual NASA Goddard Space Flight Center 
cleanroom, where they collaborate across Mechanical, Electronic, and Network engineering 
departments.
Players formulate mission objectives, balance a 150,000 dollar budget through tiered 
logistics trade studies, execute 3D precision assembly metrology, satisfy official Goddard 
engineering directives, and launch the Hubble Space Telescope into Low Earth Orbit aboard 
the Space Shuttle Discovery (STS-31). Powered by real NASA General Mission Analysis Tool 
(GMAT R2026a) orbital telemetry, Horizon-X transforms complex Concept Maturity Level 
frameworks into an engaging, collaborative WebGL experience running instantly on any 
standard browser with zero software installation
details:
Core Capability & Mission Scope: End-to-End Space Observatory Simulation

Horizon-X simulates the end-to-end lifecycle of a NASA flagship space observatory mission from ground-level cleanroom integration to orbital deployment. Inside a 3D Goddard Space Flight Center cleanroom, players inspect, test, and mount six core spacecraft subsystems: RSU-02 gyroscopic attitude canisters, solar array drive mechanisms (SADM), the DF-224 flight computer PCB, Fine Guidance Sensors (FGS), high-gain microwave antennas (HGA), and optical fiber communication links. Following subsystem certification and engineering directive evaluations, players initiate the STS-31 Space Shuttle launch simulation to deploy the telescope into Low Earth Orbit under live orbital telemetry

Concept of Operations (ConOps): The End-to-End Engineering Workflow

The application is built on a browser-native Three.js WebGL architecture:

1. Reception & Security

Players enter a 3D lobby, spawn ReadyPlayerMe astronaut avatars, and acquire security access keycards.

2. Cleanroom Navigation

Players navigate the cleanroom in first-person or third-person perspective with physical collision boundaries and aerospace Ground Support Equipment (GSE) work platforms.

3. Multidisciplinary Workbenches

The facility features three specialized engineering bays: Desk 01 (Mechanical): Mounts gyroscopes and aligns solar array drive gears. Desk 02 (Electronic): Performs solder inspections and oscilloscope voltage tuning. Desk 03 (Network): Executes waveguide torque locking and fiber optic fusion splicing.

4. Logistics Trade Studies

Implements JPL Concept Maturity Level (CML 3) trade studies where players allocate a 150,000 dollar baseline budget across Standard, Calibrated, and Flight-Grade tools based on durability limits.

5. Dual-Viewport Assembly Metrology

Renders the global spacecraft alongside magnified component inspection viewports to verify alignment tolerances.

6. Launch Simulation & GMAT Telemetry

Staging from Launch Complex 39-A through SRB separation, External Tank jettison, and orbital insertion, driven by an Earth JGM-3 geopotential gravity model and Runge-Kutta 8(9) numerical propagation.

7.  Post-Flight Audit

Evaluates six Goddard Engineering Directives (ENG-M01 to ENG-N02), scores standard compliance versus shortcut penalties, and confirms a 100 percent historical match to the authentic Hubble Space Telescope deployment

Core Value Proposition & Educational Benefits

Zero Installation

Runs natively on any modern desktop, laptop, tablet, or smartphone browser without requiring proprietary software downloads or high-end graphics processing units.

Dual-Tier Educational Accessibility

Features an Age 13+ High School mode with conceptual analogies, alongside an Advanced Systems Engineering mode with micro-inch metrology tolerances, structural torque margins, and orbital state vectors.

Real-Time Team Collaboration

WebSocket networking enables distributed multiplayer teams to divide roles across desks and assemble spacecraft concurrently

Strategic Vision & Global Educational Impact

Horizon-X democratizes aerospace systems engineering education worldwide. By converting dense NASA handbooks and orbital mechanics into interactive, collaborative gameplay, it inspires students and future engineers to pursue STEM careers and master how real NASA space observatories are designed and built.

Software, Tools & Computational Framework

  • 3D Graphics & Spatial Visualization: WebGL, Three.js
  • Frontend Core: HTML5, Modern Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), CSS3
  • Orbital Mechanics Simulation: NASA General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT R2026a)
  • 3D Astronaut Avatar Geometry: ReadyPlayerMe
  • Real-Time Networking: WebSockets, Socket.IO

Creative Approach & Gameplay Innovation

Instead of an arcade-style rocket launcher or static flashcards, Horizon-X faithfully recreates the authentic multidisciplinary cleanroom environment where hardware assembly and mathematical orbital mechanics converge. By enforcing real NASA workmanship standards and trade-study budgeting, every player decision has tangible physical consequences on the mission's flight clearance.

Systems Engineering Considerations & Architectural Trade-offs

Our team prioritized zero barrier to entry (instant web load without downloads), physical and historical accuracy (NASA GMAT ephemeris and HST STS-31 specifications), WCAG AAA color contrast compliance, and full mobile responsiveness via virtual touch controls.
